extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent practitioners (applicants, agents, attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and requirements for claiming the benefit/priority of prior U.S. and international (including provisional) applications: what must be identified, how and where to state it, timing limits, petition practice for delayed claims, and sufficiency of prior-filed disclosure under 35 U.S.C. 112(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of prior application and relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), and 386(c) must identify the prior application by application number, by international application number and international filing date, or by registration number and international filing date under 37 CFR 1.1023, and indicate the relationship between the applications (whether the instant application is a continuation, divisional, or continuation-in-part of the prior nonprovisional application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.78; identification must include both the prior application identifier and the specific relationship type. For international design applications that become nonprovisional, identifying by the nonprovisional application number is preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper phrasing of benefit claim in specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the reference to a prior nonprovisional application appears in the specification (permitted for applications filed before September 16, 2012), a proper benefit claim must state the relationship and filing date, e.g., “this application is a continuation of prior Application No. ---, filed ---.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A benefit claim that merely states “this application claims the benefit of Application No. ---, filed ---” or “is a continuing application of Application No. ---, filed ---” does not comply with 35 U.S.C. 120 and 37 CFR 1.78 because it fails to state the required relationship (continuation, divisional, or continuation-in-part).

rubrics_metrics.name: Location and form of benefit claim (ADS vs. specification) by filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012 the reference must be included in an application data sheet (ADS). For applications filed prior to that date, the benefit claim must appear either in the ADS or in the first sentence(s) of the specification following the title (or as an amendment to the first sentence(s) of the specification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 211.02; if benefit claim appears elsewhere but was recognized on the filing receipt, petition may not be required, but the claim must still be submitted in the manner specified by 37 CFR 1.78 (ADS or spec as applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive nature of relationship terms (continuation/divisional/CIP)
rubrics_metrics.description: To specify the relationship between applications, applicant must specify whether the application is a continuation, divisional, or continuation-in-part of the prior application; the terms are exclusive and an application cannot be, for example, both a continuation and a divisional or both a continuation and a continuation-in-part of the same application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claiming benefit to an entire chain of prior-filed nonprovisionals, the relationship for each link in the chain must be specified (e.g., “this application is a continuation of Application No. C, filed ---, which is a continuation of Application No. B, filed ---, which is a continuation of Application No. A, filed ---”).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued prosecution application (CPA) special rule
rubrics_metrics.description: In a CPA filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) (design applications under 35 U.S.C. chapter 16 only), a specific reference in the first sentence(s) of the specification or in an ADS to the prior application assigned the same application number is not required and may not be made; the CPA transmittal request is considered the specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No amendment in a CPA may delete the specific reference to the prior application assigned the same application number; references to applications not assigned the same number may be made when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application reference requirements and relationship omission
rubrics_metrics.description: When a nonprovisional application filed on or after September 16, 2012 claims the benefit of one or more provisional applications under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), the reference must be included in an ADS. For applications filed prior to that date the reference must be in an ADS and/or the first sentence(s) of the specification. The relationship term (continuation/divisional/CIP) is not required and should not be specified when claiming the benefit of a prior provisional under 35 U.S.C. 119(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant states that the later application “is a continuation” of a provisional or otherwise mixes 119(e) and 120 language, it may create ambiguity as to whether benefit is sought under 119(e) or 120; claiming benefit to a provisional under 120 is not recommended because it can affect patent term measurement under 35 U.S.C. 154(a)(2). Also, design applications cannot claim benefit of provisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of incomplete or improper benefit claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Any benefit claim that does not both identify a prior application by its application number and specify a relationship between the applications will not be considered to contain a specific reference as required by 35 U.S.C. 120 and may not be recognized by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not recognized, the claim may not be included on the filing receipt and publication may not be scheduled on the basis of the prior application’s filing date. If the time period set forth in 37 CFR 1.78 for submitting the required reference has expired, applicant must submit a petition under 37 CFR 1.78 and pay the petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(m) to accept an unintentionally delayed claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time period for making a benefit/priority claim (37 CFR 1.78)
rubrics_metrics.description: For utility or plant applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), the benefit claim must be made during the pendency of the application and within the later of four months from the actual filing date of the later-filed application or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior-filed application. For national-stage nonprovisionals under 35 U.S.C. 371, the benefit claim must be made within the later of: (1) four months from national stage commencement, (2) four months from the date of initial submission to enter the national stage, or (3) sixteen months from the filing date of the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This time period is not extendable; failure to submit the required reference within this time period is considered a waiver of the benefit unless a petition under 37 CFR 1.78 to accept an unintentionally delayed claim is granted. For design applications, the claim must be submitted during pendency of the later-filed application.

rubrics_metrics.name: When petition and fee are required vs. not required to correct benefit claim
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 and 37 CFR 1.78 is not submitted within the required time period, a petition for an unintentionally delayed claim under 37 CFR 1.78 and the petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(m) are required to add the benefit claim. However, a petition and fee are not required where the reference was previously submitted within the time period but not in the location specified by 37 CFR 1.78 (e.g., was included in an oath/declaration or transmittal letter) provided the information concerning the benefit claim was recognized by the Office (as shown on the first filing receipt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when a petition is not required because the Office recognized the claim, the applicant must still submit the required reference in the proper manner (ADS or amendment to first sentence(s) of specification as applicable). See MPEP § 211.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting a filing receipt with missing/incorrect benefit information
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant receives a filing receipt with missing or incorrect benefit claim information, applicant may request a corrected filing receipt, but the Office will not grant such a request to include a benefit claim unless the proper reference to the prior application is included (i) in an ADS for applications filed on or after September 16, 2012 or (ii) in the first sentence(s) of the specification or an ADS for applications filed prior to September 16, 2012, within the time period required by 37 CFR 1.78 (with some exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the proper reference was previously submitted, the request should indicate where/when it was submitted. Applicants should promptly review their filing receipts to avoid the need for a petition and associated fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding benefit claim after filing may require additional filings depending on application status
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to filing a petition under 37 CFR 1.78 (and corrected ADS/amendment), to add a benefit claim it may be necessary, depending on application status, to file: (A) a request for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114 if the application is under final rejection or has been allowed; or (B) a reissue application or a request for a certificate of correction under 37 CFR 1.323 if the application has issued as a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment or ADS filed after final rejection or allowance is not entered as a matter of right and must be filed in compliance with 37 CFR 1.116 or 1.312, respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deleting benefit claims and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may delete a benefit claim: for applications filed on or after September 16, 2012 by filing a corrected ADS deleting the reference; for applications filed prior to that date by amending the specification or submitting a supplemental ADS. A deletion of a benefit claim may be considered as evidence that the applicant intentionally waived the benefit claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should consider whether any new prior art may now be available if a benefit claim is deleted. Amendments or ADSs deleting benefit claims filed after final rejection or after allowance are treated under 37 CFR 1.116 or 1.312 respectively. If the applicant later files a petition to accept an unintentionally delayed claim after cancellation, the Office may refuse to accept it because the cancellation may show the delay was intentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference to prior application cannot be added after filing
rubrics_metrics.description: When a benefit claim is submitted after the filing of an application, the reference to the prior application cannot include an incorporation by reference statement specifying the prior application unless an incorporation by reference statement specifying the prior application was presented upon filing of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An incorporation by reference statement added after an application’s filing date is not effective because no new matter can be added after the filing date (see 35 U.S.C. 132(a)); see Dart Indus. v. Banner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content and extra-information requirement for delayed benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.78 to accept an unintentionally delayed benefit claim must be accompanied by: (1) the reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 or 119(e) and 37 CFR 1.78 to the prior application (unless previously submitted); (2) a petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(m); and (3) a statement that the entire delay between the date the benefit claim was due and the date filed was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require additional information where there is a question whether the delay was unintentional; a petition filed more than two years after the due date requires additional explanation of circumstances establishing the entire delay was unintentional (see Clarification: 85 FR 12222-24 and MPEP § 711.03(c)). Petitions for unintentionally delayed benefit claims should be forwarded to the Office of Petitions (see MPEP § 1002.02(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delayed benefit claims in international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.78 (and the petition fee) are required to add a benefit claim under 35 U.S.C. 120 and 365(c) in an abandoned international application designating the United States, even when the international application did not enter the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition under 37 CFR 1.78(c) or (e) is required in an international application that was not filed with the United States Receiving Office and is not a nonprovisional application, the petition may be filed in the earliest nonprovisional application that claims benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c)/386(c) to the international application and will be treated as having been filed in the international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure in prior-filed application (35 U.S.C. 112(a) requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be entitled to the benefit of the filing date of an earlier-filed application, the later-filed application must be an application for a patent for an invention which is also disclosed in the prior application; the disclosure in the prior application must provide adequate support and enablement for the claimed subject matter in compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112(a) (except for the best mode requirement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disclosure of the prior-filed application must provide adequate written description and enablement to permit one of ordinary skill in the art to make and use the claimed invention without undue experimentation. See Transco Prods. and case law citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application support requirements (New Railhead precedent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), the written description and drawing(s) (if any) of the provisional application must adequately support and enable the subject matter claimed in the nonprovisional application that claims the benefit of the provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In New Railhead Mfg. v. Vermeer Mfg. Co., the court held that the provisional specification must contain a written description sufficient under 35 U.S.C. 112¶1 to enable an ordinarily skilled artisan to practice the invention claimed in the nonprovisional. Lack of adequate support in the provisional can result in the nonprovisional not being entitled to the provisional’s filing date (with attendant invalidity risks under 35 U.S.C. 102/102(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims in provisional not required but later claims must be supported
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim is not required in a provisional application; however, for a claim in a later-filed nonprovisional application to be entitled to the benefit of the provisional filing date, the provisional’s written description and drawings (if any) must adequately support and enable the subject matter of that later claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the provisional does not adequately support the claim limitations present in the later-filed nonprovisional (e.g., a specific structural limitation), the nonprovisional is not entitled to the provisional filing date and the patent can be vulnerable to intervening prior art.
